question.text: Pallavi manages a Category II AIF with a corpus of INR 800 crore. Outsourced fund administration and support services (administrators and fund accountants) appointed by the AIF typically:

answer.text: Provide fund accounting, valuation and reporting, back-office support, and assistance with regulatory reporting and investor communications
Select and execute investment transactions for the AIF
Provide legal opinions on fund documentation
Conduct the annual statutory audit of the fund

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes outsourced support service providers — including administrators and fund accountants — who supply fund accounting, valuation and reporting, back-office and client-communication support, and assistance with regulatory reporting. Their fees (fund accounting, valuation, reporting) are recognised fund expenses and their work is reviewed within fund administration governance. Investment execution is the manager's role, legal opinions come from legal counsel, and statutory audit is the auditor's function. The Trap: Investment execution confuses operational support with portfolio management — outsourced administrators support the back-office, they do not take investment decisions. Note: Rewrote stem, key, and explanation around source-backed outsourced support services, fund accountants, and back-office/reporting review. Removed the over-specific Fund Administration Agreement and administrator-specific duty list (NAV computation, investor record-keeping, subscription/redemption processing) that were not directly supported in the checked workbook pages.
